title: Many-Worlds Interpretation (Everett, 1957)
description: Hugh Everett's proposal: the wavefunction never collapses — every quantum measurement branches the universe, and all outcomes occur in decohered branches. It is the most literal reading of quantum mechanics, favored by many cosmologists for its mathematical economy. Status: an interpretation, not an established fact — it makes the same predictions as Copenhagen for all current experiments.

title: Eternal Inflation — Bubble Universes
description: In eternal inflation, the inflaton field decays at different times in different regions, spawning bubble universes — each potentially with different constants — inside an ever-expanding inflating background. Guth, Linde, and Vilenkin developed the picture; it is arguably the most mainstream multiverse proposal. Status: hypothesis — it follows from inflation, but inflation itself, while strongly supported, is not proven.

title: The String Theory Landscape
description: String theory's equations admit an enormous landscape of vacuum solutions — estimates around 10^500 — each a possible universe with different particles and constants. Weinberg used anthropic reasoning on this landscape to predict the cosmological constant's observed value before it was measured. Status: hypothesis stacked on hypothesis — strings unproven, landscape unproven.

title: The Simulation Hypothesis (Bostrom)
description: Nick Bostrom's 2003 trilemma: either civilizations never reach simulation maturity, or they don't run ancestor simulations, or we are almost certainly simulated. It is philosophy, not physics — unfalsifiable as usually stated, though some propose looking for lattice artifacts in cosmic rays. Filed here as a philosophical proposal with its logic intact and its testability questioned.

title: Many-Minds Interpretation
description: The many-minds variant of Everett assigns the branching to minds rather than worlds: each observer's mind splits across outcomes while one physical world suffices. Albert and Loewer developed it to handle the probability problem in many-worlds. Status: a minority interpretation of an interpretation — doubly speculative, but a legitimate position in the literature.

title: Modal Realism (Lewis)
description: David Lewis's modal realism holds that all possible worlds are as real as the actual one — possibility is a matter of what happens at other concrete worlds. It is metaphysics, not physics, but it gives possible-worlds semantics for logic and language. Filed as philosophy: rigorous, unfalsifiable, and influential far beyond physics.

title: The Quantum Suicide Thought Experiment
description: Quantum suicide asks what many-worlds implies for the experimenter: in the branches where the gun fires, he dies; where it doesn't, he lives — so subjectively he always survives. It is a thought experiment about the meaning of probability in Everett, not an experiment to perform. Filed as a conceptual probe with its ethics and logic examined, not endorsed.

Anthropic reasoning is legitimate selection-effect logic; what it explains depends on whether a multiverse exists to select from — which is the open question.

title: The Measure Problem
description: Eternal inflation predicts infinite universes — and infinities break probability: what fraction of observers see our constants depends on how you count. Youngness paradoxes, Boltzmann brains, and cutoff-dependence show the measure problem is unsolved; without a measure, multiverse theories can't make predictions. Filed as the field's central technical embarrassment, honestly labeled.
